course_description:
The course introduces communication theories to Master of Communication students. These theories will be deployed to engage with real communication problems.

This course provides an introduction to classic theories of communication and their application in contemporary communication contexts. The goal of this course is to equip students with knowledge and understanding of key communication theories and the ability to use theory to analyse and critique communication across interpersonal, group, public and mass communication contexts.

assessment_details.title: Applying theory
assessment_details.task_description: The aim of the first assessment is to understand how theory is applied in everyday life and in research. You will choose one of the theories covered in Weeks 2 and 4 and then write a report that includes the following sections: 1) a description of the theory, 2) a description of an experience from your own life and a reflection on how the chosen theory helps to make sense of the experience, 3) a brief literature review showing how the theory is used in research. The full assessment guidelines and marking rubric will be available on the Course Blackboard site. Read full task description Hide full task description

The focus is not on memorising information, but on understanding, applying judgement, and demonstrating your own thinking.

assessment_details.title: Theoretical analysis of a communication campaign
assessment_details.task_description: The aim of this assignment is to help you to use theory to critique real world communication campaigns that seek to influence people. You will choose a communication campaign that has been conducted in Australia. Your task is to analyse the extent to which the campaign illustrates aspects of one of the public communication theories, covered in Weeks 5 to 7. Through the theoretical analysis you will draw conclusions about whether the communication campaign is likely to be successful and make recommendations for how it could have been improved. learning_activities.topic: Week 1 - Introductory Lecture An overview of the course and how it will be run will be provided. Why theory is important and traditions in communication theory will be introduced. Learning outcomes: L01
Week 1 - NO TUTORIAL Tutorial start in Week 2.
Week 2 Lecture - The self in communication The lecture will focus on theories of the self in communication - Symbolic interactionism and Expectancy violation theory. Learning outcomes: L01, L02

Week 2 Tutorial - The self in communication The Week 2 tutorial includes activities that help to understand the theories covered in the Lecture. The first assessment item will be introduced. Learning outcomes: L01, L02
Week 3 Lecture - No Lecture due to public holiday
Week 3 Tutorial - No tutorials due to public holiday

Week 4 Lecture - Developing and maintaining relationships The lecture will cover Social penetration theory & Relational dialectics theory - two theories related to developing and maintaining interpersonal relationships. Learning outcomes: L01, L02
Week 4 Tutorial - Developing and maintaining relationships Tutorial activities related to the theories covered in the lecture & assignment consultation Learning outcomes: L01, L02
Week 5 Lecture -Influencing others (1) These are the first two theories related to influencing others. The lecture will cover The Rhetoric and Framing theory. Learning outcomes: L01, L02
Week 5 Tutorial - Influencing others (1) Tutorial activities focused on the Week 5 theories. Learning outcomes: L01, L02

Week 6 Lecture - Influencing others (2) This lecture covers the second two theories related to influencing others: the Elaboration likelihood model and Cognitive dissonance. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Week 6 Tutorial - Influencing others (2) Tutorial activities focused on the Week 6 theories and Assessment guidance. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Week 7 Lecture - Influencing others (3) The lecture will cover theories that relate to the use of narratives and stories to influence others. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Week 7 Tutorial - Influencing others (3) Tutorial activities focused on the Week 7 theories and assessment guidance. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Week 8 Lecture - Mass communication (1) The lecture will focus on theories related to the effects of mass media: Media ecology theory and Semiotics. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Week 8 Tutorial - Mass communication (1) Tutorial activities focused on the Week 8 theories and assessment consultation. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Week 9 Lecture - Mass Communication (2) The lecture will focus on theories related to the effects of mass media: Cultivation theory and Agenda setting theory. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04
Week 9 Tutorial - Mass Communication (2) Tutorial activities focused on the Week 10 theories. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04
MID-SEMESTER BREAK
Week 10 Lecture - Mass communication (3) The lecture will focus on theories related to mass communication: Uses and Gratification theory and the Two-step flow theory. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04
Week 10 Tutorial - Mass communication (3) Tutorial activities related to the theories covered in the lecture. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04
Week 11 Lecture - Group and organisational communication The lecture will cover theories that relate to communication in groups and within organisations. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04
Week 11 Tutorial - Group and organisational communication Tutorial activities related to the theories covered in the lecture. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04

Week 12 Lecture - Applying theory to understand contemporary communication issues In the final lecture we will focus on a contemporary communication issue and explore how theory helps us to understand the issue. Learning outcomes: L04
Week 12 Tutorial - Applying theory to understand contemporary communication issues Tutorial activities related to the content of the lecture and exam preparation. Learning outcomes: L04
Week 13 - NO LECTURE
Week 13 - NO TUTORIAL

policies_and_procedures: University policies and procedures apply to all aspects of student life. As a UQ student, you must comply with University-wide and program-specific requirements, including the: Student Code of Conduct Policy Student Integrity and Misconduct Policy and Procedure Assessment Procedure Examinations Procedure Reasonable Adjustments for Students Policy and Procedure AI for Assessment Guide Recording of Teaching Policy and Procedure Learn more about UQ policies on my.UQ and the Policy and Procedure Library . Course guidelines Communication Expectations While you are a student at UQ, all communication must be conducted according to the UQ Student Code of Conduct . The UQ Library has a helpful Communicate and collaborate online module . Email is the primary way for you to send messages to, and receive information from, the School and our staff. You must use your UQ email address (not a private address) to communicate with staff. You should add a clear subject line, including course code, and a 2-3 word statement. You can send email at any time, however, please do not expect responses outside normal working hours (Monday to Friday from ~8am to ~5pm). Emails that constitute bullying, harassment or discrimination against staff contravene the Student Code of Conduct. Emails like this will be reported to the University, and the matter will be pursued as misconduct. Learning activities
